fields.position: Gate the current video's evidence to decide which scores can enter the fusion. Tilt provider weights using correlations between raw scores and outcomes from a completed run. Fit the table once between runs, then keep it read-only.
fields.tradeoff: The method needs a completed reference run and its correlations depend on the VideoAlign proxy, not independent emotion preferences. CPU tests cover allocation only; they do not execute visual scorers or full generation training.

fields.title: Fuse the video reward, or allocate it across generation tokens?
fields.body: EmoReward calibrates one scalar per video across score providers, using current validity and proxy correlations from a completed run. TVRL redistributes an existing group advantage along the generation-token axis using input gradients from a frozen VLM. A scalar does not identify which tokens caused an effect; a gradient attribution does not estimate whether facial or motion providers remain reliable across runs. Control the provider set and credit allocator separately in comparisons.

fields.question: If two videos have the same final emotion scalar, must EmoReward and TVRL assign the same credit to their generation tokens?
fields.answer: No. EmoReward outputs a video-level scalar, not token credit. TVRL distributes an existing group advantage using gradients from a frozen VLM. Two videos with the same scalar can have different token sensitivities. Attribution cannot create nonzero credit when the underlying group advantage is zero.
fields.example: Teaching example: Suppose both videos have positive advantages in one group. Foreground movement matters more in one video, while a later transition matters more in the other. TVRL sensitivities can differ; EmoReward does not emit that allocation.

fields.summary: Added EmoReward from the November 5 bulletin overlap. Comparing it with TVRL separates provider correlation, current validity, and within-group token sensitivity. The CPU L1 component runs neither the generator nor full training.
